propositions: When two divergent bundles exist for a single ref on S3, git ls-remote returns ambiguous heads and clone fails with 'multiple updates for ref not allowed', making the store unclonable and push retriable but unresolvable.

The upstream git-remote-s3 Doctor.fix_multiple_bundles is interactive-only (blocking input() prompts) and by default discards the non-chosen head's events, causing irreversible data loss from the append-only event log.

The heal must use iterated 2-parent lossless merges (never octopus, never merge=union) following rebar's existing sync._union_merge semantics to safely union divergent bundle heads without discarding unique events.

The heal acquires the helper's per-ref S3 lock, re-enumerates bundles for TOCTOU protection, fetches all divergent heads, merges them under rebar's write_lock, writes the merged bundle before deleting originals, and never deletes the merged result — guaranteeing at least one lossless bundle at every crash point.

The heal is invoked from push.py when _is_multi_bundle detects the multi-bundle signature, guarded by healed_once to prevent retry loops, and reuses git-remote-s3's S3Remote/.s3 client (boto3 transitive under [s3] extra, no new core dependency).

Concurrent doctors serialize via the helper's acquire_lock; a process unable to acquire the lock (another repair in flight) backs off, waits for the winner's collapse, and converges on the single healed bundle — no reinvented lock marker, no corrupt duplicate repair.
